newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek rates idle, equilibrium seen restored Weds.
newsitem.headline: Greek rates idle, equilibrium seen restored Weds.

text.p: Greek depos and forex swaps were little changed in late unexciting trade hovering around morning levels amid expectations that forex-linked liquidity will restore interest rate equilibrium on Wednesday.

"There will be more liquidity in the system tomorrow and it is very likely to see the central bank on the bid-side and the overnight drop," said a foreign bank trader. "Rates hold morning levels and trading activity is light."
The Bank of Greece injected overnight cash again today at an unchanged 13.40 percent to satisfy the demand from cash starved banks.

Other traders said the market was bracing for stable to slightly lower interest rates in the money and bond markets until year-end given the resistance put up by inflation. CPI inflation was flat at 8.5 percent year-on-year in September.
"The outlook is for stable to marginally lower interest rates by year-end," said a dealer."Inflation seems to be stuck."
Dealers said it appeared less likely that there would be an FRN auction before December given the state's huge cash reserves estimated around 1.0 trillion drachmas.

"The treasury is full of cash. I do not think an FRN auction will take place before December," said a senior money market dealer at a private bank. "Auctions of three-and five-year securities with fixed coupons or purely discount bonds might take place in te interim."
About 300 million ecus, 100 million marks and $65 million were sold at the fixing, dealers said on Tuesday.
The mark was quoted at 157.11/21 drachmas from Tuesday's 157.250 fix, the dollar at 239.72/82 drachmas from 240.750 and the Ecu at 300.39/49 from 300.800 drachmas.
